steps: A planing operation is performed on a Planer for 57 minutes to transform a milled part into a planed part, with a cut depth of 0.5 mm, a feed rate of 0.2 mm/rev, and a surface finish of Ra 1.6 µm, with both input and output components conveyed on the ConveyorBelt.

A tapered broach is used on a Broaching Machine to broach a Metal bar for 18 minutes at a feed rate of 0.15 mm/rev and a depth of cut of 10 mm, resulting in a Broached component that is transferred to a ConveyorBelt.

The milling with precision grinding operation is performed on the Stewart Platform Mills for 44 minutes, converting a milled part from the ConveyorBelt into a ground part also on the ConveyorBelt using a 5-axis end mill with a milling precision of ±0.01 mm and an active damping system to control vibrations.

Surface Grinding is performed on a Grinding Machines using an Aluminum oxide wheel at 3000 rpm with a feed rate of 0.1 mm/rev, processing a Planed part on the ConveyorBelt for 17 minutes to produce a Ground part on the ConveyorBelt.

On a Vertical Lathe, a MetalBar is lathe turned for 66 minutes at a rotation speed of 800 rpm using a Carbide turning tool with a feed rate of 0.1 mm/rev, resulting in a LathedPart that is transferred to a ConveyorBelt.

The wire electrical discharge machining operation is performed on a Wire EDM (Electrical Discharge Machine) for 34 minutes using a molybdenum wire with pulse on time of 5 µs, pulse off time of 100 µs, voltage of 60 V, and a cutting speed of 0.05 mm/min, transforming a shaped part on the conveyor belt into a precision finished ground part that remains on the conveyor belt.

The sheet metal is laser cut on the Laser Cutter for 83 minutes at a laser power of 2 kW, a cutting speed of 15 mm/s, and with nitrogen gas assist at 15 bar, producing a cut sheet metal on the ConveyorBelt.

A Bandsaw Cutting operation is performed for 76 minutes using a carbide-tipped blade at a saw speed of 1000 rpm and a cutting width of 20 mm, transforming a Metal Bar input carried by a MobileRobot into a Lathed part output conveyed to a ConveyorBelt.

A drilling operation is performed on a Metal bar using a Drill Press for 66 minutes at a spindle speed of 1200 rpm, a feed rate of 0.1 mm/rev, and a drill size of 6 mm, resulting in a DrilledComponent being transferred to the ConveyorBelt.

On the Screw Machines, a lathed part is processed for 20 minutes using Screw Thread Machining to create a screw thread with an M6 size and metric trapezoidal thread type, resulting in a screwed component that is transferred to a mobile robot.

The CNC Turning and Finishing operation is performed on a CNC Turning Center for 94 minutes using a Standard finish program, with tool offsets calibrated to 0.005 mm and a spindle speed of 1000 rpm, starting with a lathed part on the ConveyorBelt and producing a finished machined component classified as a MilledPart that is then conveyed back to the ConveyorBelt.

The honing operation is performed on a Honing Machine for 67 minutes using a 60 grit honing tool to finish a honed cylinder with a bore size of 50 mm, resulting in a precision finished part that is transferred to the ConveyorBelt.

A horizontal milling operation is performed on a Horizontal Milling Machine for 76 minutes using a contour cutting path at a milling speed of 1500 rpm to achieve a surface finish of Ra 0.8 µm, starting with a milled part on a conveyor belt and producing a finished machined component on the same conveyor belt.

The shaping operation is performed on a shaper for 1 minutes using a carbide tool with a stroke length of 150 mm and a shaping speed of 0.5 mm/rev, converting a milled part on the conveyor belt into a shaped part that is then conveyed out on the conveyor belt.

Shearing of sheet metal on the Shear (Sheet Metal) machine for 84 minutes using a high-carbon steel blade at a cutting speed of 12 m/min and a shear angle of 90 degrees, transforming the input sheet metal on the ConveyorBelt into sheared sheet metal also on the ConveyorBelt.

Punching is performed on a Punch Press for 31 minutes using a 10 mm punch size, a stroke speed of 150 mm/s, and automatic die alignment, starting with sheet metal on a conveyor belt and ending with a finished sheet metal product transferred to a mobile robot.
A Vertical Milling Machine mills a lathed part for 78 minutes at a milling speed of 1200 rpm using an end mill with a depth of cut of 3 mm, transforming the lathed part into a milled part.

A broached component is hobbed on a Hobbing Machine for 16 minutes at a hobbing speed of 800 rpm and a feed rate of 0.1 mm/rev to produce a hobbied gear with a standard involute gear profile, with the input component fed on the ConveyorBelt and the output hobbied gear exiting on the ConveyorBelt.

A spur gear with 24 teeth is shaped on a Gear Shaper for 91 minutes at a shaping speed of 100 mm/min, starting from a broached component on the ConveyorBelt and producing a shaped gear on the ConveyorBelt.

A Vertical Turning operation is performed on a Vertical Lathe for 3 minutes using a Single-point tool with a rotation speed of 800 rpm and a feed rate of 0.15 mm/rev, converting a Metal bar from the ConveyorBelt into a Lathed part which is then placed back on the ConveyorBelt.

The planing operation is performed on a Planer for 77 minutes to reduce the surface of a milled part by 2 mm with a feed rate of 0.5 mm/min, achieving a surface finish of Ra 6.3 μm, resulting in a planed part that is stored on the StorageCart.

Surface Grinding is performed on a Grinding Machines using an Aluminum oxide wheel at 3000 rpm and a feed rate of 0.1 mm/rev, processing a Planed part from StorageCart to produce a Ground part stored in FinalStorage for 81 minutes.
A Bandsaw performs sawing on a Metal bar to produce a Lathed part, operating for 43 minutes at a saw speed of 800 rpm using a high-carbon steel blade with a cutting width of 50 mm.

Roughing milling is performed on a Stewart Platform Mill for 65 minutes using a 3-axis end mill with a 4-flute cutter to achieve a milling precision of ±0.05 mm, with the active damping system engaged, transforming a milled part carried by a mobile robot into a ground part also carried by the mobile robot.

The sheet metal is laser cut on the Laser Cutter for 68 minutes at 1500 W laser power, 12 m/min cutting speed, with nitrogen assist at 15 bar, producing a cut sheet metal that remains on the ConveyorBelt.

A shaping operation is performed on a shaper for 61 minutes using a carbide tool with a 10° bevel, with a stroke length of 120 mm and a shaping speed of 80 mm/min, starting with a milled part held by a mobile robot and ending with a shaped part transferred to a conveyor belt.

A drilling operation is performed on a Metal bar using a Drill Press for 69 minutes at a spindle speed of 1200 rpm, a feed rate of 0.2 mm/rev, and a drill size of 6 mm, resulting in a DrilledComponent that is transferred to a MobileRobot.

A CNC Turning operation is performed on a CNC Turning Center for 26 minutes using a standard gear profile program, with tool offsets set to 0.02 mm from datum and spindle speed at 1800 rpm, starting with a lathed part on a conveyor belt and producing a finished machined component as a milled part that is transferred to a mobile robot.

Punching is performed on a Punch Press for 47 minutes using a 10 mm diameter punch with automatic die alignment maintained within 0.01 mm tolerance and a stroke speed of 150 mm/sec, processing sheet metal input on a conveyor belt to produce a finished sheet metal product on the same conveyor belt.

A broached component is hobbed on a Hobbing Machine for 87 minutes at a hobbing speed of 600 rpm and a feed rate of 0.1 mm/rev to produce a Hobbied gear with a standard 20° involute profile, transitioning from the MobileRobot to the ConveyorBelt.

A spur gear with 24 teeth is shaped on a Gear Shaper for 53 minutes at a shaping speed of 40 mm/min, starting from a broached component held by a MobileRobot and ending as a shaped gear conveyed to a ConveyorBelt.

On a Vertical Lathe, a MetalBar is lathe turned for 81 minutes at a rotation speed of 600 rpm using a Carbide turning tool with a feed rate of 0.15 mm/rev, resulting in a LathedPart being transferred to a MobileRobot.

On a Horizontal Lathe, a Metal bar is lathe turned for 59 minutes at a rotation speed of 500 rpm using a high-speed steel tool with a feed rate of 0.1 mm/rev to produce a Lathed part that is then conveyed out on the ConveyorBelt.

The grinding operation, performed on Grinding Machines using an aluminum oxide wheel at 3000 rpm with a feed rate of 0.05 mm/rev, processes a planed part carried by a mobile robot and produces a ground part that is transferred to a conveyor belt for a duration of 81 minutes.

Shearing of sheet metal on the Shear (Sheet Metal) machine for 80 minutes using a high-strength cold-rolled steel blade at a 45° shear angle and a cutting speed of 20 m/min, starting with sheet metal on a conveyor belt and producing sheared sheet metal delivered to a mobile robot.

The honing operation is performed on a Honing Machine for 63 minutes to finish a honed cylinder component on a conveyor belt, using a 60 grit honing tool with a 50 mm bore size and a cycle time of 30 seconds per pass, resulting in a precision finished part that is transferred to a mobile robot.

A milled part is planed on a Planer for 31 minutes at a planing depth of 2 mm, a feed rate of 1.5 mm/min, and a surface finish of Ra 1.6 µm, resulting in a planed part that is conveyed to the ConveyorBelt.

A broaching operation is performed on a Broaching Machine for 21 minutes using a tapered broach for internal keyway with a feed rate of 0.3 mm/rev and a depth of cut of 15 mm, starting with a Metal bar on a ConveyorBelt and producing a Broached component that is transferred to a MobileRobot.
On the Screw Machines, a lathed part is screwed using an M6 coarse thread screw for 46 minutes to produce a screwed component, which is then transferred to a mobile robot.

A vertical milling operation is performed on a Vertical Milling Machine for 3 minutes using an end mill with 3 flutes at a milling speed of 1500 rpm and a depth of cut of 3 mm, transforming a lathed part on a conveyor belt into a milled part that is then transferred to a mobile robot.

A horizontal milling operation is performed on a Horizontal Milling Machine for 82 minutes using a milling speed of 1200 rpm, following a contour path with 5-axis interpolation to achieve a surface finish of Ra 3.2 μm, starting with a milled part held by a mobile robot and ending with a finished machined component transferred to a conveyor belt.

A wire EDM cutting operation is performed on a shaped part conveyed on a conveyor belt, using a molybdenum wire with a pulse duration of 50 ns, peak current of 15 A, and a cutting speed of 1.2 mm/min, for 64 minutes, to produce a precision finished part that is transferred to a mobile robot.
